title: Cover Picture and Issue Information
content:
Cover image: Ectomycorrhizas on a fine tree root, viewed under a stereomicroscope. Each pale, swollen tip marks where a soil fungus has wrapped around the root, trading mineral nutrients for plant sugars (Credit: Benjamin Underwood © RBG Kew).

This cover is provided by the authors of the article Ectomycorrhizal community composition and extramatrical hyphal proportion predict soil carbon stocks at the landscape scale (https://doi.org/10.1111/1365-2435.70369), which features in this issue. They identified fungi from over 3500 ectomycorrhizal roots, and characterised composition, diversity, abundance, and morphological traits (hyphae and rhizomorphs) and related these to soil carbon stocks. Their findings demonstrate that ectomycorrhizal community composition predicts soil carbon storage at landscape scales, and suggest that integrating fungal data into ecological prediction frameworks can improve carbon monitoring and management.
